target_customer: Startup founders and finance teams managing cap tables and equity
problem: Founders misestimate ownership and dilution and pay high legal fees; cap table tools were dominated by Carta.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription (Startup $1,200 per year, Growth $3,500 per year, Enterprise custom)

founders.name: Yin Wu
education: Stanford, computer science, dropped out in 2011
founders.background_notes: YC page says she sold her previous company to Microsoft in 2015 and is a three-time YC alumna (S11, S13, W20); Fortune says 2013 sale. Date conflict noted.

founders.name: Grant Oladipo
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page with no bio.

exit.reason: Company site announces shutdown on 12/8/26 and points customers to Carta; no reason given publicly.

competitors.name: Carta
competitors.what: Dominant cap table and equity platform

competitors.name: Shareworks (Morgan Stanley)
competitors.what: Enterprise equity compensation platform, formerly Solium
competitors.funding_then: Morgan Stanley bought Solium for $900M in 2019

technical_complexity.rationale: Cap table modeling and equity grants are well understood CRUD and finance logic, with correctness and compliance as the hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Cap table data creates some lock-in but Carta had the network of investors and law firms; Pulley competed on price and modeling.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Carta stayed the category leader; Pulley announced a shutdown in September 2026 effective December 8, 2026 with customers assisted to Carta.

market_need_then: Fortune Oct 2020 reported Yin Wu learned she owned about 10% less than assumed after her earlier sale, motivating tools that model dilution; customers included Fast and Clubhouse.

identity.voice_and_tone: founder-friendly, positioned as modern challenger to Carta

branding.community_and_virality: Founder angel list was strong (Stripe, Elad Gil, Parker Conrad, Jack Altman) but no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Short real-word name and Fortune framing as Carta rival with Stripe backing; no evidence of brand-driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Pulley challenged Carta with Stripe-backed funding, raising $10M in 2020 and $40M in 2022, but announced in September 2026 that it will shut down on December 8, 2026 and refer customers to Carta. The cause is not public, so failure factors are left empty; a competitor led the category throughout.
notes: Directory status says Active but the company site announces shutdown on 12/8/26; exit type shutdown with date as scheduled. Series B 2022-07 $40M led by Founders Fund comes from search summaries of aggregator and profile pages (total about $50M matches); no primary article opened. Fortune names Echo Lockscreen sold in 2013, YC page says 2015. Shutdown reason is not public; founder reportedly said it was not the outcome wanted (secondary).
